reason: The Description textarea carries aria-invalid=true and aria-errormessage pointing at an existing span, and Chrome exposes both (invalid=true, errormessage=Please complete this field), so its state and value are programmatically determinable. What is missing is redundancy: the span is not in a live region or aria-describedby, so a screen reader with weak aria-errormessage support may not read it on focus. aria-errormessage is optional ARIA and the submit-time announcement gap is the 4.1.3 finding, so the 4.1.2 impact is minor.

The Spend limit per person input carries aria-invalid=true and aria-errormessage pointing at an existing span, and Chrome exposes both (invalid=true, errormessage=Amount must be greater than 0). Its aria-describedby points at a help-text id that does not exist, so the error is carried by aria-errormessage alone and may go unread in screen readers with weak support. aria-errormessage is optional ARIA and the submit-time announcement gap is the 4.1.3 finding, so the 4.1.2 impact is minor.

reason: Reproduced from cards.create-budget: with focus on Next, pressing Enter inserts "Please complete this field" under Description, outside any live region, alert or status role. A MutationObserver saw all three errors added with no live ancestor, focus stayed on Next, and the page's only role=alert div stayed empty. A screen-reader user hears nothing and must hunt for the errors; this is 4.1.3, and it is not a money movement, so it stays medium.
